section.title: Two Ways to Solve Quadratic Equations
section.para: In the activity, Han and Jada used two different methods for solving a quadratic equation, using the distributive property and the square root property.
section.title: Using the Distributive Property to Solve Quadratic Equations

para.emphasis: How to Solve a Quadratic Equation Using the Distributive Property:

div.para: Step 1 -Isolate the quadratic term and make its coefficient 1.
Step 2 -Rewrite the term so the binomial is multiplied by itself.
Step 3 -Use the distributive property or FOIL.
Step 4 -Combine like terms so that the equation is set equal to 0.

section.para:
Step 1 - Isolate the quadratic term (divide by 4).
\((x-7)^2=9\)

Step 2 - Rewrite the term so the binomial is multiplied by itself.
\((x-7)(x-7)=9\)

Step 3 - Use the distributive property or FOIL.
\(x^2-7x-7x+49=9\)

Step 4 - Combine like terms so that the equation is set equal to 0.
\(x^2-14x+40=0\)

Step 6 - Set each factor equal to 0.
\(x-10=0\), \(x-4=0\)
section.title: Try It: Using the Distributive Property to Solve Quadratic Equations

problem.para: Use the distributive property to solve \(3(x-4)^2=48\).
Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Here is how to solve the quadratic equation using the distributive property.

Step 1 - Isolate the quadratic term (divide by 3).
\((x-4)^2=16\)

Step 2 - Rewrite the term so the binomial is multiplied by itself.
\((x-4)(x-4)=16\)

Step 3 - Use the distributive property or FOIL.
\(x^2-4x-4x+16=16\)

Step 4 - Combine like terms so that the equation is set equal to 0.
\(x^2-8x=0\)

Step 6 - Set each factor equal to 0.
\(x=0\) or \(x-8=0\)

section.title: Using the Square Root Property to Solve Quadratic Equations

para.emphasis: How to Solve a Quadratic Equation Using the Square Root Property:

div.para: Step 1 -Isolate the quadratic term and make its coefficient one.
Step 2 -Use the square root property. Take the square root of both sides of the equation and remember the "plus or minus."
Step 3 -Rewrite the equation as two equations.

section.para:
Step 1 - Isolate the quadratic term (divide by 4).
\((x-7)^2=9\)

Step 2 - Use the square root property.
\(\sqrt{(x-7)^2}=\sqrt{9}\)
\(x-7=\pm 3\)

Step 3 - Rewrite the equation as two equations.
\(x-7=-3\)
\(x-7=3\)
section.title: Try It: Using the Square Root Property to Solve Quadratic Equations

problem.para: Use the square root property to solve \(3(x-4)^2=48\).
Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Here is how to solve the quadratic equation using the square root property:

Step 1 - Isolate the quadratic term (divide by 3).
\((x-4)^2=16\)

Step 2 - Use the square root property.
\(\sqrt{(x-4)^2}=\sqrt{16}\)
\(x-4=\pm 4\)

Step 3 - Rewrite the equation as two equations.
\(x-4=4\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;x-4=-4\)
